help.tips[0].examples[0].en: I wanted to take the bus in the morning, but I was too late.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: The bus left right in front of my nose.
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: Modal verbs stay in the Präteritum even when you tell a story aloud; the action verb hat geregnet is in the Perfekt.
help.tips[0].en.text: war, hatte and the modals (wollte, konnte, musste) → Präteritum, even in speech. Everything else → Perfekt: ist abgefahren, habe gewartet, hat angehalten. This mix is normal spoken German, not an error.
help.tips[0].en.title: Spoken narrative mixes the tenses
help.tips[0].en.trap: English uses one past tense for everything ('I waited, I was late'). German speech switches: ich habe gewartet, but ich war zu spät.
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: First I waited at the stop for ten minutes.
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: Luckily a neighbour stopped in her car.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: A signpost in position 1 is followed directly by the verb, then the subject.
help.tips[1].en.text: Letzte Woche / Neulich · Zuerst · Dann · Plötzlich · Zum Glück · Leider · Unterwegs · Seitdem · Am Ende. One per sentence keeps the listener with you — and after a signpost in position 1, the verb comes next.
help.tips[1].en.title: Signposts of the story
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: Something funny happened to me last week.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: So in the end the missed bus was a real stroke of luck.
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: A good story opens with a hook that promises something; Am Ende and Seitdem are closing lines.
help.tips[2].en.text: Mir ist neulich etwas Lustiges / Peinliches / Seltsames passiert … — and end with a one-line point or a Seitdem-sentence.
help.tips[2].en.title: Open with a hook, close with a point
help.hookEn: Tell a short story out loud the way Germans do, from Letzte Woche to Am Ende, and keep your listener with you.
help.introEn: Twelve sentences that tell one small story — a missed bus, a rain shower and a lucky lift — to listen to and repeat with the stress and rhythm of spoken narrative. Two things to imitate. First, the time words that carry the listener along: Letzte Woche, Zuerst, Dann, plötzlich, Zum Glück, Unterwegs, Seitdem, Am Ende. Second, the tense mix Germans actually use when they tell a story aloud: war, hatte, wollte, mussten stay in the Präteritum (Ich wollte den Bus nehmen, aber ich war zu spät), while the action verbs are in the Perfekt (Der Bus ist abgefahren, ich habe gewartet, eine Nachbarin hat angehalten). Written stories use the Präteritum throughout; spoken ones sound like this. Practise until the story runs without a pause between sentences; that flow is what makes a listener stay with you.
help.rememberEn[0]: war / hatte / wollte / musste in the Präteritum, actions in the Perfekt.
help.rememberEn[1]: Zuerst – dann – plötzlich – zum Glück – am Ende.
help.examEn: Telling a short personal experience with clear time signposts is a standard speaking task in the B1 exam — and at every dinner table.
